mainTopic: The גורל for the goats of יום הכיפורים, and רב חסדא's rule on when the birds of a קן are designated, with two challenges
overview: This עמוד first finishes an earlier argument. An anonymous ספרא follows רבי יהודה, and it says only the גורל makes the goat a חטאת. So for רבי יהודה the הגרלה is indispensable, and the opposing view is refuted. Next, רב חסדא rules that the two birds of a קן get their roles only at the owner's taking (לקיחה) or at the כהן's offering (עשייה), and רב שימי בר אשי gives the פסוקים behind this. The גמרא challenges רב חסדא from the ברייתא about the גורל, which seems to picture naming at the time of the lottery. רבא answers that the ברייתא only imagined naming at לקיחה or עשייה. A second challenge comes from a poor מטמא מקדש who became rich and then divided his money. רב ששת answers that, according to רבי הושעיא, the division must have happened while he was still poor, at the setting aside, which counts as לקיחה. The גמרא then asks about the opposing view of רבי יאשיה, and that question continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The anonymous ספרא is רבי יהודה, so for him the lottery is indispensable
steps.stepSummary: An unnamed ספרא follows רבי יהודה. It teaches that only the גורל makes the goat a חטאת. So for רבי יהודה, the הגרלה is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who wrote the unnamed statements in the ספרא? רבי יהודה. And the ספרא teaches: the lottery makes the goat a חטאת, but just naming it a חטאת does not. So clearly the lottery is indispensable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds a proof to settle an earlier argument about whether, for רבי יהודה, the הגרלה is required for the goats of יום הכיפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule that an anonymous statement in the ספרא follows רבי יהודה. This ספרא says only the גורל can make the goat a חטאת, and saying the name does not. So the lottery cannot be skipped, which means it is מעכב.

keyTerms.meaning: An anonymous statement in the ספרא (the halachic מדרש on ויקרא)
Who is it? Who is the author?
The lottery used to choose the goat לה׳ and the goat לעזאזל
Verbally naming or designating it (here, calling it a חטאת)
Apparently; this shows that
Is indispensable; without it the מצוה is invalid

steps.confusionAlert: Here "הַשֵּׁם" does not mean God's Name. It means verbally naming the animal as a חטאת.

and it teaches:
The lottery makes it a sin-offering,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (end of the previous דף) about רבי יהודה's view on whether הגרלה is מעכב.
steps.raayaObject: That for רבי יהודה the הגרלה is indispensable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The anonymous ספרא: הגורל עושה חטאת ואין השם עושה חטאת, together with the rule that an anonymous ספרא follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The view that the lottery is not indispensable is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The proof is a full refutation of the opinion that the הגרלה is not מעכב, and the גמרא accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of the one who says the lottery is not indispensable. It is indeed a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא declares that the opposing view has been refuted, and closes this argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some said that for רבי יהודה the lottery is not indispensable. The ספרא proves the opposite. The word תיובתא, said a second time, means the refutation stands and there is no answer.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation. When repeated, it means a conclusive refutation.
The one who says (an opinion)

steps.whatToRemember: Final result: for רבי יהודה, the גורל is indispensable for the goats of יום הכיפורים. Only the lottery, not a verbal name, makes the goat a חטאת.

phrases.english: This is a refutation of the one who says
that the lottery is not indispensable.
It is indeed a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from the proof in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The view that הגרלה is not מעכב (for רבי יהודה) is refuted.

steps.title: רב חסדא: bird pairs are designated only at taking or at offering
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that the two birds of a קן get their roles (one חטאת, one עולה) only when the owner takes them or when the כהן offers them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The birds of a קן become set apart for their specific offering only in one of two ways: when the owner takes them, or when the כהן performs the offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new, related topic. It asks when the birds of a קן become designated for their roles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some people must bring a pair of birds, one as a חטאת and one as an עולה. רב חסדא says each bird's role can be fixed at only two points: when the owner acquires them, or when the כהן actually offers them. This suggests that a verbal naming at any other time does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Nests: pairs of birds brought as one חטאת and one עולה
Become designated; get their specific roles
The owner's taking (buying or acquiring) of the birds
The כהן's performance of the offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the comparison to the goats of יום הכיפורים: what designates an offering, and does saying a name count?

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Nests become designated only
either upon the owner's taking,
or upon the priest's performance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אֵין הַקִּינִּין מִתְפָּרְשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new but related subject: how offerings are designated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Birds of a קן receive their designation only at the owner's taking or at the כהן's performance.

steps.title: The verses behind רב חסדא's rule
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי explains that רב חסדא's source is the two פסוקים "ולקחה" and "ועשה."
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי said: What is רב חסדא's reason? It is written "and she shall take" and "and he shall offer." So designation happens either at the taking or at the offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי gives the פסוקים that support רב חסדא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק describes the owner taking the birds for their roles ("ולקחה"). Another describes the כהן offering them for their roles ("ועשה"). Since the תורה mentions only these two moments, these are the only points where designation happens.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
As it is written
"And she shall take" (ויקרא יב:ח)
"And he shall offer" (the כהן's act, ויקרא טו:טו)

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi said:
What is the reason of Rav Chisda?
As it is written: "And she shall take," "And he shall offer."
Either at the taking, or at the performance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural basis for step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words ולקחה and ועשה limit designation to the taking or the offering.

steps.title: Challenge to רב חסדא from the lottery ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא from the ברייתא saying "the גורל makes a חטאת, the שם does not."
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: "And he shall make it a חטאת". The lottery makes it a חטאת, but naming does not make it a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב חסדא. This step sets up the problem. The ברייתא continues in step 6, the challenge is spelled out in step 7, and רבא answers in step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that, without the פסוק, we would have thought naming could make the goat a חטאת. Its קל וחומר seems to picture naming at the moment of the lottery. That moment is neither לקיחה nor עשייה, the only two times רב חסדא allows. Step 7 spells this out.

keyTerms.meaning: "And he shall make it a חטאת" (ויקרא טז:ט)

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same ברייתא used in step 1, but for a new purpose. There it proved the lottery is indispensable. Here it challenges רב חסדא about birds.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
"And he shall make it a sin-offering,"
the lottery makes it a sin-offering,
but the naming does not make it a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב חסדא's ruling from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that קינין are designated only at taking or at performance.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's first assumption is that naming at the time of the lottery could have fixed the goat's role. That moment is neither לקיחה nor עשייה, so naming would work outside רב חסדא's two moments (spelled out in step 7).

steps.title: The ברייתא's קל וחומר and the verse that rejects it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a קל וחומר: naming should make the goat a חטאת. The פסוק "ועשהו חטאת" teaches that only the גורל does, not the שם.
steps.simpleTranslation: A verse is needed, because I might have thought: is it not logical? There is a case where a lottery does not make the animal holy, the birds of a קן, and still naming does. So in the goats' case, where the lottery does make them holy, shouldn't naming surely work too? That is why the verse says "and he shall make it a חטאת": the lottery makes it a חטאת, but naming does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its quote of the ברייתא that it started using against רב חסדא. Quoting the full ברייתא sets up the actual challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא builds a קל וחומר. With birds, a גורל has no power, yet naming them works. With the goats of יום הכפורים, a גורל does have power, so naming should work even more. The פסוק blocks this and says only the גורל can make the goat a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not logical? This opens a קל וחומר.
Made holy, gave the animal its sacred status
The naming, a verbal designation such as "this is a חטאת"
The verse comes to teach (us otherwise)
"And he shall make it a sin-offering" (ויקרא טז)

steps.confusionAlert: Here "השם" does NOT mean God's Name. It means the act of naming, saying out loud "this one is a חטאת."

phrases.english: For I might have thought: is it not logical?
phrases.notes: We're still in the middle of the ברייתא that started back in step 5.

phrases.english: If, in a case where the lottery does not consecrate,
phrases.notes: This is the birds of a קן.

phrases.english: naming does consecrate,
then in a case where the lottery does consecrate,
phrases.notes: This is the goats of יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: isn't it logical that naming should consecrate?!
Therefore the verse says: "And he shall make it a sin-offering":
the lottery makes it a sin-offering,
but naming does not make it a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quotation of the ברייתא that step 5 brought as a challenge to רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule (step 3) that the birds' roles are set only at לקיחה or עשייה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's הוה אמינא treats naming as a real option for the goats. The next step shows why that clashes with רב חסדא.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא contradicts רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא pictures naming at the time of the lottery. That is neither לקיחה nor עשייה, yet the ברייתא still thought naming could fix the animal's role.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, at the lottery, it is not the time of taking and not the time of offering. Yet the ברייתא teaches that naming would set the role.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out exactly how the ברייתא contradicts רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lottery happens at neither of the two moments רב חסדא allows, לקיחה or עשייה. Still, the ברייתא assumed that naming at that moment could have worked, if not for the פסוק. This suggests naming can work at other times too, which goes against רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: The time of taking (buying or acquiring) the animals
The time of doing, when the כהן offers the קרבן
Fixed or set, permanently establishes the role
And yet it teaches

phrases.english: But here,
which is not the time of taking
and not the time of offering,
and yet it teaches that naming would set the role!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the contradiction out of the ברייתא quoted in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's limit to לקיחה or עשייה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's הוה אמינא assumes naming at the lottery could work. So naming would be effective outside לקיחה and עשייה, which contradicts רב חסדא.

steps.title: רבא rereads the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the ברייתא's הוה אמינא differently. It was about naming at the time of לקיחה or עשייה, not naming at the time of the lottery.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, this is what the ברייתא means. Take the birds: there a lottery does nothing, even if held at taking or offering time, yet naming at taking or offering time works. Now take the goats: there a lottery works even though it is not at taking or offering time. Isn't it logical that naming at taking or offering time should work too?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. The ברייתא never suggested naming during the lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's reading, the קל וחומר compares the powers of the גורל and the שם, but the naming always happens at לקיחה or עשייה. The gap in timing is only about the גורל. So the ברייתא fits רב חסדא's rule that naming works only at those two times.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (a reinterpretation)
And even
Not at the time of

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's rule survives. Naming the birds of a קן works only at לקיחה or עשייה. The ברייתא's הוה אמינא was also only about naming at those times, and the פסוק says that for the goats only the גורל works anyway.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that "שם" has a fixed time window. The ברייתא does not widen it. It only compares how strong naming is against the גורל.

phrases.english: Rava said: this is what it means:
If, in a case where the lottery does not consecrate,
even at the time of taking,
and even at the time of offering,

phrases.aramaic: קִידֵּשׁ הַשֵּׁם בִּשְׁעַת לְקִיחָה וּבִשְׁעַת עֲשִׂיָּיה,
phrases.english: naming does consecrate at the time of taking and the time of offering,
then in a case where the lottery does consecrate,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁעַת לְקִיחָה וְשֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁעַת עֲשִׂיָּיה,
phrases.english: even though it is not at the time of taking or offering,
isn't it logical that naming should consecrate
at the time of taking and the time of offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by reinterpreting the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא imagined naming at the time of the lottery, outside לקיחה and עשייה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא imagined naming only at לקיחה or עשייה. Only the גורל was the one acting outside those times. So the ברייתא does not contradict רב חסדא.

steps.title: רבא finishes his reading: only the lottery makes a sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his explanation. The ברייתא's קל וחומר (about naming at לקיחה or עשייה) is rejected by the פסוק 'ועשהו חטאת': only the גורל makes the goat a חטאת, not the שם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And he shall make it a sin-offering.' The lottery makes it a sin-offering, but the name does not make it a sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: This line ends רבא's answer from the last step. It quotes the פסוק that blocks the ברייתא's קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's reading, the ברייתא first thought that naming at לקיחה or עשייה should work for the שעירים, just as it works for birds. The פסוק 'ועשהו חטאת' teaches that for the שעירים only the גורל decides. This fits רב חסדא well: naming works for birds only at לקיחה or עשייה, and for the goats not at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (comes to reject a wrong assumption)
'And he shall make it a sin-offering' (ויקרא טז:ט)
The name, meaning a spoken designation

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the ברייתא never imagined naming at the time of the lottery. So רב חסדא's rule (naming works only at לקיחה or עשייה) survives the challenge.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'And he shall make it a sin-offering,'
the lottery makes it a sin-offering,
but the name does not make it a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's reinterpretation of the ברייתא begun in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the ברייתא's הוה אמינא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The challenger thought the ברייתא imagined naming at the time of the lottery, which would show that naming works even outside לקיחה and עשייה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא imagined naming at לקיחה or עשייה, and the פסוק rejects even that for the שעירים. Nothing in it contradicts רב חסדא.

steps.title: A new source: the poor person who became rich
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a poor מטמא מקדש. He set aside money for his bird pair, became rich, and then divided the money into חטאת money and עולה money. He may add to the חטאת money for his new obligation, but not to the עולה money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a poor person entered the מקדש while impure. He set aside money for his pair of birds, and then he became rich. Afterward he said: 'These coins are for my sin-offering, and these are for my burnt-offering.' He may add money and bring his required offering from the sin-offering money. He may not add money and bring his required offering from the burnt-offering money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge to רב חסדא by quoting a ברייתא. This step lays out the case. The next step shows why it is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מטמא מקדש brings a קרבן עולה ויורד, an offering that depends on his money. A poor person brings two birds, one as a חטאת and one as an עולה. A rich person brings an animal חטאת. Once he became rich, his obligation is an animal חטאת. He can use the money he named for the חטאת toward it, but the money he named for the עולה is locked as עולה money.

keyTerms.meaning: One who entered the Temple while impure
His 'nest': his pair of birds offered as קרבנות
He became wealthy
His required offering (here, an animal חטאת)
His burnt-offering

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge reads the ברייתא as saying he split the money only later, after he was already rich. That timing is the whole point of the challenge. רב ששת will reject this reading in steps 12–13.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
a poor person who made the Temple impure,
and he set aside money for his bird pair, and he became rich,
and afterward he said:
'These are for my sin-offering, and these are for my burnt-offering' —
he adds and brings his obligation from the money of his sin-offering,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מוֹסִיף וּמֵבִיא חוֹבָתוֹ מִדְּמֵי עוֹלָתוֹ.
phrases.english: but he does not add and bring his obligation from the money of his burnt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered by רבא, a new source is brought against רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that bird offerings get their roles only at לקיחה or עשייה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats a later verbal division of the money as binding. The next step makes this explicit.

steps.title: The naming here fixed the money outside the allowed times
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the challenge. The man's naming happened neither at לקיחה nor at עשייה, yet the ברייתא treats it as fixing the money's role. That contradicts רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, this is not the time of taking and not the time of offering, and yet the ברייתא teaches that the naming fixed the role!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states why the ברייתא is a problem for רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said naming fixes a bird offering's role only at לקיחה (when the owner buys or takes it) or at עשייה (when the כהן offers it). Here the owner named the money at a third time, after setting it aside and before buying any birds. Since the עולה money cannot be moved to the חטאת, the naming clearly worked. So naming can work even outside רב חסדא's two moments.

keyTerms.meaning: The time of taking or buying the offering
The time of the כהן performing the offering
It fixed (permanently set the role)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a direct attack on the core of רב חסדא's position. רב ששת answers it in steps 12–13.

phrases.english: But here,
which is not the time of taking
and is not the time of performing,
and yet it teaches that it fixed the role!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא, דְּלָאו שְׁעַת לְקִיחָה וְלָאו שְׁעַת עֲשִׂיָּיה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the contradiction out of the ברייתא quoted in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's limitation of naming to לקיחה or עשייה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids using the עולה money for the חטאת, which proves the naming took effect. The naming happened neither at לקיחה nor at עשייה, so naming can work outside רב חסדא's two moments.

steps.title: רב ששת questions how the ברייתא was read
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת rejects the idea that the man divided the money after he became rich. According to רבי הושעיא, a rich man cannot fulfill his obligation with a poor man's offering, so a naming made at that point could not fix anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Do you really think so? רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי הושעיא: a rich מטמא מקדש who brought a poor man's offering has not fulfilled his obligation. If he cannot fulfill his obligation with it, how could his naming fix the money's role?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת steps in to defend רב חסדא. He says the challenge read the ברייתא the wrong way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the man divided the money into חטאת and עולה after he became rich. But a rich man's bird offering does not count at all, according to רבי הושעיא. So a naming made while he was rich could never 'fix' the money's role. The reading behind the challenge therefore cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And do you really think so?' This opens a rejection of the way the questioner understood things.
The cheaper offering a poor person brings (two birds) instead of an animal.
He has not fulfilled his obligation.
Fixed or set the role of the money for good.

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת is not attacking רב חסדא. He is defending him by attacking the way the challenge read the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
And do you really think so?
phrases.notes: He's pushing back on the idea that the division happened after the man became rich.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Elazar say in the name of Rabbi Hoshaya:
a wealthy person who made the Temple impure
and brought a poor man's offering has not fulfilled his obligation.
And since he does not fulfill his obligation with it,
how could his naming fix the money's role?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: וְתִסְבְּרָא? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the challenge from Step 11 by rejecting the timeline it assumed.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It rejects the assumption that the man divided the money after he became rich.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A rich man cannot fulfill his obligation with a poor man's offering, so a naming made while rich could not fix the money's role.

steps.title: The division happened while he was still poor, at the setting aside
steps.stepSummary: Everyone must agree that the man divided the money while he was still poor. So the division happened at the time he set the money aside (הפרשה), which counts as לקיחה. This fits רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must you say? That he already named the money while he was poor. Here too, then, he named it already at the time he set it aside.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives the correct reading of the ברייתא. In that reading, the ברייתא no longer contradicts רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the naming could only work while he was poor, it must have been made back then, when he first set the money aside. Setting the money aside counts as לקיחה. So the naming happened at לקיחה, which is exactly when רב חסדא says naming fixes the role.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, what must you say?' This introduces the only reading that works.
From the time he was poor.
Here too; the same idea applies.
The moment the money was set aside. This counts as לקיחה.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's naming happened when the poor man set the money aside, which counts as לקיחה. So the ברייתא does not contradict רב חסדא. Step 14 then tests this answer against the opinion of רבי יאשיה.

phrases.english: Rather, what must you say?
That he had already named it while he was poor.
Here too:
he had already named it at the time he set the money aside.
phrases.notes: Setting the money aside counts as לקיחה, so this fits רב חסדא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This completes רב ששת's answer that began in Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: It changes when we understand the naming in the ברייתא to have happened.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The man named the money after becoming rich, which is neither לקיחה nor עשייה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The man named the money while still poor, at הפרשה, which counts as לקיחה. So the ברייתא is consistent with רב חסדא.

steps.title: What about the opinion that a rich man does fulfill his obligation?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises רבי חגא's report in the name of רבי יאשיה: a rich man who brings a poor man's offering does fulfill his obligation. This weakens רב ששת's answer, and the challenge continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי חגא, who said in the name of רבי יאשיה that he does fulfill his obligation...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge. It brings an opinion that disagrees with the one רב ששת relied on, and the question finishes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת's answer depended on רבי הושעיא's view that a rich man's poor-offering does not count. According to רבי יאשיה, it does count. Then the man could have named the money after he became rich, and the contradiction with רב חסדא comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And according to רבי...' This introduces a different opinion to test the answer.
He has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not finished here. This line only sets it up, and the question continues on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Chaga, who said in the name of Rabbi Yoshiya,
who said that he does fulfill his obligation,
phrases.notes: The question continues on the next עמוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי חַגָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה, דְּאָמַר יָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This challenges רב ששת's answer by bringing an opinion that disagrees with the source he relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's answer, which depends on רבי הושעיא's ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a rich man's poor-offering does count, as רבי יאשיה holds, then naming the money after becoming rich could fix its role. That brings back the contradiction with רב חסדא.
